title: A node is READY only when its HARD dependencies are ACCEPTED: the surface blocks on depends:<nodeKey>
description:
SPIDR child 2 of parent task-4423d2a4c3084d579c132b253d36b502 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-04). dependsOn child 1 task-f79d38b119984ae1ae51eba887a28b7d: without a sealed multi-node graph there is nothing for this gate to gate.

This is the parent's DoD 5' from owner ruling comment-fbe64776: "a node.deliver step is READY only when every dependsOn node is ACCEPTED; otherwise the surface lists it BLOCKED with missing: [\"depends:<nodeKey>\", ...]".

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb:
- THE GAP IS REAL. `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts:363-410` loops sealed nodes and derives status from the REVIEW LEDGER ALONE (accepted -> COMMITTED; replanned -> BLOCKED ["replan"]; >=3 unsuccessful rounds -> BLOCKED ["escalation"]; clean round awaiting the verifier -> BLOCKED [verification tokens]; otherwise READY). The word `dependsOn` does not appear in the file. Every un-accepted node of an approved plan is offered READY at once, so the wrapper would staff a dependent node beside its parent.
- THE FACT IS ALREADY IN THE SEALED GRAPH - no core or scheduler change is needed. `apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.ts:220` seals per-node `dependsOn`; it lands in `GraphRevisionContent` two ways: `content.snapshot.edges` (GraphEdge[], `packages/scheduler/src/graph-model.ts:41-45`) and `content.nodeAuthority.definitions[].directHardDependencies` (`packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-authority-contract.ts:162-168`).
- THE READ IS ALREADY WRITTEN ONCE, in a sibling module: `apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts:98-104` derives a node's dependencies as `edges.filter((edge) => edge.consumerNodeKey === definition.nodeKey)`. REUSE that derivation rather than inventing a second one; a second spelling is how the board and the surface come to disagree about build order.
- THE CARRIER TO EXTEND: `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-contract.ts:30-33` `interface NodeSpec { nodeRef; title }`. It is produced at `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/compiled-node-source.ts:178-179` (`sealed().map(node => ({nodeRef: node.nodeKey, title: node.objective}))`) from the local `SealedNode` (compiled-node-source.ts:111-116), which today drops dependencies. Both need the new member.
- THE MISSING-TOKEN VOCABULARY IS IN THE BROWSER, NOT THE DAEMON: `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/work-labels.ts` (198 lines) maps each token to operator words ("escalation", "verification", "verifier-policy", "replan"). A `depends:<nodeKey>` token is PREFIXED, unlike every existing exact-match token - read how the map is keyed before adding, and handle the prefix form explicitly.
- ALREADY DONE, DO NOT REBUILD: the BOARD already renders build order. `apps/control-room/src/v2/board/board-columns.ts:73` prints `after ${node.dependsOn.join(", ")}` for a QUEUED node and `board-lanes.tsx:77` shows a "Depends on" field, both fed by `/runs/read`'s dependsOn through `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts:62`. This row must not re-derive that.
definitionOfDone: `NodeSpec` (apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-contract.ts) carries the node's HARD dependencies, and `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/compiled-node-source.ts` populates it from the sealed graph using the SAME derivation runs-read.ts:98-104 uses (edges filtered by consumerNodeKey, or directHardDependencies) - not a second hand-rolled walk. A test seals a 3-node chain and asserts the produced NodeSpec dependency lists match the submitted dependsOn exactly.

apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts marks a node.deliver step BLOCKED with `missing` containing `depends:<nodeKey>` for EVERY dependency whose review is not ACCEPTED, and READY only when all are accepted. The test asserts the exact token strings (not just that missing is non-empty) and asserts the dependent node is NOT among nextAllowedCommands' review.submit offers while blocked.

Precedence is pinned by test: a node that is both dependency-blocked AND awaiting verification/escalation/replan reports a deterministic, asserted `missing` set - the architect does not care which order, but the test names it so the wrapper's behaviour cannot drift silently. A node with zero dependencies behaves exactly as today (regression arm asserting READY).

The transitive case is covered: in a->b->c chain with only a ACCEPTED, b is READY and c is BLOCKED on `depends:b`. Assert both in one test so a gate that only reads direct parents of the frontier cannot pass.

apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/work-labels.ts gives `depends:<nodeKey>` operator words naming the blocking node, and its test asserts the rendered sentence for a real token. Bidirectional roster check (global rail 9): every token the daemon can emit has a label AND every label corresponds to an emittable token - assert set-equality, enumerating the daemon side from the emitting seam, not from the label map.

Mutation drill recorded in a step note: make the gate ignore dependencies (return READY unconditionally) in affordance-read.ts, confirm the `depends:` token test and the transitive test both go RED, restore, prove the restore with `git diff` on the tracked file (quote the empty diff).
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: ACCEPTED means the review ledger's accepted record, the same fact affordance-read.ts:366-371 already uses to mark a node COMMITTED. Do not invent a second notion of doneness (landing receipt, verifier receipt) for this gate - a node is a satisfied dependency exactly when the surface would call it COMMITTED.

SHAPE CHANGE ALERT (global rail 19): adding a member to NodeSpec and a token to `missing` changes returned shapes that tests assert as literals. Before editing, grep for literal `missing: []` expectations, `nodes: () => [{...}]` fixtures (affordance-read.test.ts:191/623/688, affordance-read-planning.test.ts:641/836/854/858/916/921) and any hard-coded step counts; every asserting consumer must be in this row's affectedFiles or the row must be split.

implementationPlan.description: CARRY THE DEPENDENCIES ONTO THE SURFACE CONTRACT. (a) apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-contract.ts:30-33 `interface NodeSpec { nodeRef; title }` gains `readonly dependsOn: readonly string[]` — REQUIRED, not optional. An optional member defaulting to `[]` is exactly how this gate would become vacuous: if compiled-node-source forgot to populate it every node would read "no dependencies" and the gate would pass while gating nothing. Required means the compiler names every site that must supply it. (b) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/compiled-node-source.ts populates it: its local `SealedNode` (:111-116) and the `nodes()` mapping (:178-179) currently drop dependencies. Use the SAME derivation apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts:103-104 already uses — `edges.filter((edge) => edge.consumerNodeKey === definition.nodeKey).map((edge) => edge.producerNodeKey)` — reading `graph.content.snapshot.edges`. Do NOT hand-roll a second walk: the board renders build order from runs-read's version, and two spellings are how the board and the surface come to disagree about what blocks what. (c) A test in compiled-node-source.test.ts seals a 3-node chain and asserts the produced NodeSpec dependency lists EQUAL the submitted dependsOn, per node — not merely that the field is present.

DEPENDENCIES NOW RIDE ON THE SURFACE CONTRACT.

(b) compiled-node-source.ts: local `SealedNode` (:111-117) gains `dependsOn`; `sealedNodesOf` now destructures `const { edges, nodes: snapshotNodes } = graph.content.snapshot` and derives `dependsOn: edges.filter((edge) => edge.consumerNodeKey === definition.nodeKey).map((edge) => edge.producerNodeKey)` — the SAME expression runs-read.ts:103-104 already uses, not a second walk. `nodes()` (:184-186) now emits `{dependsOn, nodeRef, title}`, freezing a copy of the array so a NodeSpec consumer cannot mutate the sealed node's list.

implementationPlan.description: TESTS FIRST FOR THE GATE, in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.test.ts. Run RED. (a) DIRECT BLOCK: a 2-node graph where b dependsOn a and a is NOT accepted — assert b's step is BLOCKED and its `missing` contains the EXACT string `depends:a` (assert the literal token, not merely that missing is non-empty), and assert b is NOT among nextAllowedCommands' review.submit offers while blocked. (b) RELEASE: once a's review IS accepted, b becomes READY on the next read. (c) TRANSITIVE: an a->b->c chain with ONLY a accepted — b is READY and c is BLOCKED on `depends:b`. Assert BOTH in one test, so a gate that only looks at the frontier's direct parents cannot pass. (d) NO-DEPENDENCY REGRESSION: a node with `dependsOn: []` behaves exactly as today (READY). (e) PRECEDENCE: a node that is BOTH dependency-blocked AND awaiting verification reports a deterministic asserted `missing` set — the architect does not mandate which order, but the test must NAME it so wrapper behaviour cannot drift silently later.
implementationPlan.note:

Placed at the tail deliberately: the arms above drive this suite's shared store to a durably approved plan AND install both standing verifier slices, and the escalation/replan describes already reuse it the same way. Node keys are unique to this block (node-dep-*) so their review ledgers cannot be crossed with the node-code-1/2 worlds.

The five reds are exactly the five dependency arms, and their failure text shows the surface answering READY where BLOCKED was demanded — e.g. the precedence arm's diff was literally the missing token:
      "missing": [
    -     "depends:node-dep-c",
          "verification",
      ],
FAILING: blocks a dependent node on depends:<nodeKey> ... | gates the WHOLE chain ... | names EVERY unaccepted dependency ... | does not treat a dependency outside the sealed roster as satisfied | PRECEDENCE ...
PASSING (and they must pass in BOTH states — that is their job): "releases the dependent node the moment its dependency is ACCEPTED" and "leaves a node with no dependencies exactly as it was".

THE ARMS.
(a) DIRECT BLOCK. Pair a(-)->b. Asserts b is `{kind: "node.deliver", missing: ["depends:node-dep-a"], status: "BLOCKED"}` — the EXACT token string, since the browser reads it and a rename that kept `missing` non-empty would still break the operator. Also asserts b is offered NOTHING (`offeredKindsFor(...) === []`), which is DoD 2's "not among review.submit offers": the wrapper staffs from the offers, so leaving review.submit would staff b beside its parent. THE CONTROL is in the same arm: a is READY and IS offered review.submit, so the assertion measures the gate rather than a dead surface.
(b) RELEASE. `accept(A)` then a is COMMITTED, b is `{missing: [], status: "READY"}` and offered review.submit again.
(c) TRANSITIVE, both facts in ONE arm as the plan requires: chain a(accepted)->b->c; b READY, c BLOCKED on `depends:node-dep-b`. A gate that resolved only the frontier's direct parents would call c READY, because c's parent b IS listed — the fact it must read is that b is not ACCEPTED.
(d) NO-DEPENDENCY REGRESSION: a `dependsOn: []` node is READY with review.submit offered, exactly as before.
(e) PRECEDENCE, pinned so it cannot drift: a node with a clean round in (awaiting the verifier) AND an unaccepted parent reports `["depends:node-dep-c", "verification"]` — dependencies FIRST, verification after, and it is offered nothing.

TWO ARMS BEYOND THE PLAN'S FIVE, both cheap and both closing a way the gate could be almost-right:
- FAN-OUT: a node depending on TWO unaccepted nodes names BOTH tokens in listed order. A gate that stopped at the first unmet dependency would pass every other arm in this block.
- DANGLING DEPENDENCY: a node depending on a key that is in NO sealed roster stays BLOCKED and names it. This is step 7(c)'s adversarial question answered as an executable arm rather than prose — it is the one case where guessing "satisfied" silently un-gates a node, so it is pinned as fail-closed.

implementationPlan.description: IMPLEMENT THE GATE in apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts (428 lines — keep the addition tight; the node loop is at :363-410). Inside the per-node loop, before the existing READY branch, resolve each of the node's `dependsOn` entries against the review ledger and emit `depends:<nodeKey>` into `missing` for EVERY dependency whose review is not accepted, marking the step BLOCKED when any is. ACCEPTED means exactly what the loop already uses at :366-371 to mark a node COMMITTED — `review.accepted !== undefined`. Do NOT invent a second notion of doneness (landing receipt, verifier receipt) for this gate: a node is a satisfied dependency precisely when the surface would call it COMMITTED (task rail 1). Keep the existing replan/escalation/verification branches and their tokens intact; this step ADDS a reason a node can be blocked, it does not reorder the others. Step 4 goes green.
implementationPlan.note:
THE GATE IS IN. Step 4's five reds are green; nothing else moved.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. Two additions inside the `config.nodes !== undefined` block of `readSurface`:

1. An acceptance resolver in front of the per-node loop:
     const acceptedByRef = new Map<string, boolean>();
     const isAccepted = (nodeRef) => { ...readReviewLedger(...).accepted !== undefined... };
   ACCEPTED is `review.accepted !== undefined` — the SAME expression the loop already uses at the COMMITTED branch. No second notion of doneness was invented (task rail 1): a node is a satisfied dependency exactly when this surface would call it COMMITTED, so the board and the gate cannot come to mean different things by "done".
   The map is memoised per READ, not across reads: a surface read must be a consistent snapshot, and re-reading the ledger for a node named by three dependents would be three folds of the same events. Each node also seeds its own entry from the ledger it already read at the top of the loop (`acceptedByRef.set(spec.nodeRef, ...)`), so a node listed before its dependents costs zero extra reads.

2. In the final branch only:
     const unmet = spec.dependsOn.filter((nodeRef) => !isAccepted(nodeRef))

If a cycle can seal, this gate deadlocks rather than refuses — that is a follow-up row, not something to patch here.
